concerns.text: User Story US-1 has functional requirements (FR-001, FR-002, FR-003) but no Success Criteria are linked; there is no SC‑XXX that references US-1.
User Story US-2 is anchored by FR-004 (and FR-003) but lacks any Success Criteria; no SC‑XXX cites US-2.
User Story US-4 includes acceptance scenarios and is referenced by SC-004, yet no functional requirement (FR‑XXX) is tied to US-4.
User Story US-5 is referenced by SC-005 but has no functional requirement associated; no FR‑XXX mentions US-5.

The specification does not require verification that the external Music Emotion Rating (MER) dataset provides a validated musical‑emotion measurement instrument. The idea assumes a validated self‑report scale; without an explicit FR to confirm construct validity, the behavioral measure’s validity is under‑specified.

FR-001 requires matching subjects across the HCP resting‑state fMRI dataset and an external Music Emotion Rating (MER) dataset using the HCP Subject ID or a deterministic key based on demographics. The specification provides no evidence that the external MER dataset contains overlapping IDs or that demographic‑based deterministic matching can reliably identify the same individuals. This unverified assumption makes the behavioral outcome (MER score) not truly independent of the neural predictors and threatens the core validity of any reported brain‑behavior relationships.

The spec treats the MER construct as a single ‘MER total score’ (BehavioralScore) without confirming that the source dataset uses a validated musical‑emotion rating instrument or that the total score is psychometrically sound. Lack of construct validity for the behavioral measure means any observed correlations could reflect measurement artefacts rather than genuine brain‑behavior links.
